explanation.text:
(Pro. 29:1-27)

hardeneth . . . neck--obstinately refuses counsel (Kg2 17:14; Neh 9:16).

destroyed--literally, "shivered" or "utterly broken to pieces."

without remedy--literally, "without healing" or repairing.

bsb.text: A man who remains stiff-necked after much reproof will suddenly be shattered beyond recovery.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 11:10; Pro 28:28).

in authority--(Compare Margin), increased in power.

bsb.text: When the righteous flourish, the people rejoice, but when the wicked rule, the people groan.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 4:6-7; Pro 10:1, etc.).

bsb.text: A man who loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but a companion of prostitutes squanders his wealth.

explanation.text:
by judgment--that is, righteous decisions, opposed to those procured by gifts (compare Pro 28:21), by which good government is perverted.

land--for nation.

bsb.text: By justice a king brings stability to the land, but a man who exacts tribute demolishes it.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 26:28).

spreadeth . . . feet--By misleading him as to his real character, the flatterer brings him to evil, prepared by himself or others.

bsb.text: A man who flatters his neighbor spreads a net for his feet.

explanation.text:
In--or, "By"

the transgression--he is brought into difficulty (Pro 12:13), but the righteous go on prospering, and so sing or rejoice.

bsb.text: An evil man is caught by his own sin, but a righteous one sings and rejoices.

explanation.text:
considereth--literally, "knows," as Psa 1:6.

the cause--that is, in courts of justice (compare Pro 29:14). The voluntary neglect of it by the wicked (Pro 28:27) occasions oppression.

bsb.text: The righteous consider the cause of the poor, but the wicked have no regard for such concerns.

explanation.text:
Scornful men--those who contemptuously disregard God's law.

bring--(Compare Margin), kindle strife.

turn away wrath--that is, "abate wrath."

bsb.text: Mockers inflame a city, but the wise turn away anger.

explanation.text:
contendeth--that is, in law.

whether . . . laugh--The fool, whether angry or good-humored, is unsettled; or referring the words to the wise man, the sense is, that all his efforts, severe or gentle, are unavailing to pacify the fool.

bsb.text: If a wise man goes to court with a fool, there will be raving and laughing with no resolution.

explanation.text:
bloodthirsty--(Compare Margin), murderers (Psa 5:6; Psa 26:9).

hate, etc.-- (Pro 1:11; Gen 3:4).

seek . . . soul--that is, to preserve it.

bsb.text: Men of bloodshed hate a blameless man, but the upright care for his life.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 12:16; Pro 16:32).

mind--or, "spirit," for anger or any ill passion which the righteous restrain.

bsb.text: A fool vents all his anger, but a wise man holds it back.

explanation.text: His servants imitate him.

bsb.text: If a ruler listens to lies, all his officials will be wicked.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 22:2).

deceitful man--literally, "man of vexations," an exactor.

the Lord . . . their eyes--sustains their lives (Sa1 14:27; Psa 13:3); that is, both depend on Him, and He will do justice.

bsb.text: The poor man and the oppressor have this in common: The LORD gives light to the eyes of both.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 20:28; Pro 25:5). Such is the character of the King of kings (Psa 72:4, Psa 72:12).

bsb.text: A king who judges the poor with fairness—his throne will be established forever.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 13:24; Pro 23:13).

bsb.text: A rod of correction imparts wisdom, but a child left to himself disgraces his mother.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 29:2, Pro 29:12; Psa 12:1-8).

shall see . . . fall--and triumph in it (Psa 37:34-38; Psa 58:10-11).

bsb.text: When the wicked thrive, rebellion increases; but the righteous will see their downfall.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 29:3, Pro 29:15; Pro 19:18).

give thee rest--peace and quiet (compare Pro 29:9).

bsb.text: Discipline your son, and he will give you rest; he will bring delight to your soul.

explanation.text:
no vision--instruction in God's truth, which was by prophets, through visions (Sa1 3:1).

people perish--(Compare Margin), are deprived of moral restraints.

keepeth the law--has, and observes, instruction (Pro 14:11, Pro 14:34; Psa 19:11).

bsb.text: Where there is no vision, the people cast off restraint; but blessed is he who keeps the Law.

explanation.text:
A servant--who lacks good principle.

corrected--or discovered.

will not answer--that is, will not obey.

bsb.text: A servant cannot be corrected by words alone; though he understands, he will not respond.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 21:5).

hasty in . . . words?--implying self-conceit (Pro 26:12).

bsb.text: Do you see a man who speaks in haste? There is more hope for a fool than for him.

explanation.text: become his son--assume the place and privileges of one.

bsb.text: A servant pampered from his youth will bring grief in the end.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 15:18). Such are delighted by discord and violence.

bsb.text: An angry man stirs up dissension, and a hot-tempered man abounds in transgression.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 16:18; Pro 18:12).

honour . . . spirit--or, "such shall lay hold on honor" (Pro 11:16).

bsb.text: A man’s pride will bring him low, but a humble spirit will obtain honor.

explanation.text:
hateth . . . soul--(Compare Pro 8:36).

heareth cursing-- (Lev 5:1), risks the punishment, rather than reveal truth.

bsb.text: A partner to a thief hates his own soul; he receives the oath but does not testify.

explanation.text:
The fear . . . snare--involves men in difficulty (compare Pro 29:6).

shall be safe--(Compare Margin; Pro 18:10).

bsb.text: The fear of man is a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is set securely on high.

explanation.text: (Compare Margin; Psa 27:8). God alone will and can do exact justice.

bsb.text: Many seek the ruler’s favor, but a man receives justice from the LORD.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 3:32). On last clause, compare Pro 29:16; Psa 37:12.

Next: Proverbs Chapter 30

bsb.text: An unjust man is detestable to the righteous, and one whose way is upright is detestable to the wicked.
